newsitem.title: UK: UK engineering export orders slump in Q2 - EEF.
newsitem.headline: UK engineering export orders slump in Q2 - EEF.

text.p: Export orders among British engineering firms fell to the lowest level for three years in the second quarter as the effect of the strong pound hit home, a leading business survey said on Tuesday.
The Engineering Employers' Federation (EEF) said its latest Engineering Trends survey showed a further pronounced reduction in the volume of new export orders.
The balance of firms reporting an increase in business fell to -10 percent from -2.0 percent in the first quarter, the lowest balance in the survey's three year history.
"The balance of firms reporting an increase in total new order intake weakened markedly in the second quarter and is now only marginally positive at +3.0 percent," the survey said.
"This continues a trend established in the previous quarter as a result of slowing order export intake."
Output slackened sharply in the second quarter following a more gradual decline in the previous three months.

The balance of firms reporting an increase was +11 percent compared with +20 percent in the previous quarter. The proportion of firms reporting that they were at a satisfactory full rate of operation declined to 35 percent from 37 percent in the first quarter and is at the lowest level for 15 months.
The balance of firms reporting increased employment fell to two percent from 10 percent in the first quarter, and capital expenditure plans fell to +11 percent from +19 percent in the first quarter.
Alan Armitage, head of economics at the EEF, said the effects of the pound's rally were now being felt.
"Not only are we seeing the continuing effects of a strong pound on UK exporters, but there are also signs that the effects are working down the UK supply chain."
Armitage added that the prospects for the rest of the year depend "crucially on the level of sterling and a renewed drive for competitiveness".
